title: 關於把妹 你必須知道的真相

timeline.summary: Mikey introduces money, appearance and romance as three conventional explanations for attraction that he intends to dispute.
Money is framed as a tool rather than attraction; Titanic and a provider-versus-lover dichotomy are used to argue that gifts and support cannot create desire.
He describes a manipulative provider dynamic and narrates an identifiable suicide and marriage case with specific financial allegations.
He contrasts provider and hunter/lover identities, then uses bird and human-evolution claims to present female dual mating strategy as biological inevitability.
Money is repositioned as a means to realize one's own value; he claims attraction based on money is replaceable while instinctive attraction produces devotion.
The appearance section rejects looks as the main cause of attraction and proposes hunter body, confidence, decisiveness and intelligence as ancestral signals.
He attributes male appearance anxiety to media and capital, then argues that shame about looks suppresses other strengths and lowers self-worth.
The romance section presents a sequence of attraction first and gifts or confession later, arguing that behavior is interpreted through pre-existing liking.
He describes a three-part consumer-capital mechanism involving demographic scarcity, moral shaming and elevation of ordinary women, without supplying evidence.
He closes the first stage of the series by encouraging confidence, self-direction and resistance to conventional judgment.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: Money, appearance and romance can affect conditions but do not, in his framework, constitute the core of male attraction.
claims.conditions: A recurring conceptual framework also present in mikey-gameshengjing-001; this upload does not validate it empirically.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: He divides men into providers who use money or pleasing behavior and lovers or hunters who generate attraction through strong behavior signals.
claims.conditions: Binary and gendered model that can obscure mixed motives, care, reciprocity and individual differences.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: He claims some women strategically extract resources from provider men, delay sex and then choose a different lover.
claims.conditions: Unsupported group-level accusation and sexual transaction model; cannot be used to classify a partner or interpret a refusal.

claims.speaker: Mikey discussing an identifiable case
claims.statement: He narrates a short marriage, large financial demands, prior marriages and a husband's suicide as evidence of deliberate exploitation.
claims.conditions: High-impact reputational, financial and suicide-related claims; the sampled visuals do not authenticate records or establish the full case.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: He uses alleged bird paternity rates and ancestral hunting pressures to claim women biologically prefer strong, dominant and resource-producing men.
claims.conditions: Species analogy, number and evolutionary causal chain are unsourced in the video and cannot be generalized to women or individual relationships.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: He proposes that appearance shame can cause a man to discount his other qualities, become anxious during interaction and create a feedback loop of low self-worth.
claims.conditions: Potential self-reflection model only; the surrounding claim that feminism and capital created a male-appearance tyranny is unsupported.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: His sequence is value or attraction first, then interest signals such as gifts or confession; he argues that the same behavior is interpreted more positively after attraction exists.
claims.conditions: Does not make harmful behavior acceptable, guarantee attraction or eliminate the need for respect and consent.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: He alleges that capital promotes demographic panic, shames men who do not spend and elevates ordinary women in order to create a profitable pleasing economy.
claims.conditions: Broad social and demographic conspiracy claim without sources or causal evidence.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: He encourages men to keep confidence and self-definition instead of letting appearance trends or another person's approval determine total self-worth.
claims.conditions: Only the narrow self-worth theme is separable; it must not carry over the video's entitlement, dominance or group claims.

examples.summary: Titanic is used as a fictional contrast between expensive provision and attraction, but a film plot cannot establish a universal relationship mechanism.
The identifiable marriage and suicide case is presented through narration and brief edited imagery; no primary financial, court or family records are shown in the reviewed material.
A hunter-body and hunter-wisdom list is used to connect fitness, confidence, decisiveness and intelligence to ancestral survival.

speaker_attribution.speaker: Mikey
speaker_attribution.basis: Single self-identified studio narrator across the main program.

speaker_attribution.speaker: public figures, film characters and social-media subjects
speaker_attribution.basis: Appear only in edited clips, photos or Mikey's narration; their motives and words are not independently established.

speaker_attribution.speaker: unmapped inserted voices
speaker_attribution.basis: Brief film or television excerpts were not continuously reviewed and are not treated as Mikey's direct statements.

visual_findings: All 23 sparse frames were reviewed. Most show Mikey speaking, with inserted street footage, phone imagery, a small case graphic, animal/film material and television excerpts.

The phone and case-related text around roughly 225-300 seconds is too small or edited to authenticate the narrated allegations; a denser review would improve source classification but not independently prove the case.
The frame around the start of the appearance section contains a small document-like overlay whose exact source and text are not readable enough for factual use.
Sparse frames do not establish continuous editing context or the accuracy of the public-case, bird-paternity, demographic or consumer-capital claims.

permissions.reason: Combines unverified identifiable-person allegations, unsupported gender/evolutionary generalizations and potentially adversarial relationship framing.

limitations: Automatic transcript was not checked word-for-word against original audio and contains repeated corruptions of names and technical terms.
Twenty-three 45-second frames are sparse screening, not continuous audio-visual verification.
The public case, animal statistic, demographic number, media-effects and capital-intent claims were not externally verified.
The provider/lover binary and repeated same-channel versions are doctrine, not independent evidence.
No statement in this source overrides another person's refusal, autonomy or right to change their mind.
